mainTopic: Releasing a vow because of a later event (נוֹלָד), the destruction of the בית המקדש, and the משנה of travelers who vow נזירות depending on an approaching stranger.
overview: The end of the משנה teaches that a vow of נזירות made after the person's animal was already stolen is not binding, because it rested on a mistake. The משנה then tells how נחום המדי wrongly released נזירים who arrived from the exile and found the בית המקדש destroyed. The חכמים ruled that anyone who vowed before the destruction stays a נזיר. In the גמרא, רבה says the חכמים won over רבי אליעזר, who had allowed opening a vow with a נולד (a later development). רבא adds that the חכמים still allow opening with the 'condition of a נולד': 'If someone had told you the Temple would be destroyed, would you have vowed?' רב יוסף suggests opening from a פסוק in ירמיהו that hints the Temples would fall. The גמרא answers that no one knew when, and even with אביי's פסוק in דניאל, no one knew the exact day. A new משנה then brings travelers who vow נזירות depending on who an approaching person is, with three opinions: בית שמאי, בית הלל and רבי טרפון. It also covers the case where the person turns back, where רבי שמעון disagrees. The גמרא questions בית הלל's wording, and רב יהודה corrects it: only the one whose words came true is a נזיר.

steps.title: A vow made after the animal was stolen is not binding
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its case: if the person became a נזיר after his animal had already been stolen, he is not a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he made the vow of נזירות after his animal was stolen, he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes a case about a man who vowed to be a נזיר, planning to bring his קרבנות from a certain animal. Here it rules that if the animal was already stolen when he vowed, the vow does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His vow depended on having that animal, but the animal was already gone when he spoke. So the vow was a mistake from the very start. This contrasts with the earlier half of the case: if the theft came after the vow, he stays a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: he took a vow of נזירות
he is not a נזיר; the vow does not take hold

phrases.english: But if he vowed nezirus after his animal was stolen —
he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's before/after split, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of nezirus made after the animal was already stolen is void, because it was a mistake from the start.

steps.title: The story of נחום המדי's mistaken release
steps.stepSummary: נחום המדי asked returning נזירים whether they would have vowed had they known the בית המקדש was destroyed. When they said no, he released them.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was the mistake that נחום המדי made. When נזירים came up from the exile and found the בית המקדש destroyed, נחום המדי asked them: 'If you had known that the בית המקדש was destroyed, would you have vowed?' They said, 'No.' So he released their vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story that shows someone getting this rule wrong. נחום המדי released נזירים because of something that happened after they had vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These נזירים vowed while the בית המקדש was still standing. Its destruction was a new event that came later. נחום treated them like the man whose animal was already gone at the time of his vow. He failed to tell apart an event before the vow from an event after it.

keyTerms.meaning: the exile (the lands outside ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: And this is the mistake that Nachum the Mede made:
When nazirites came up from the exile
and found the Temple destroyed,
Nachum the Mede said to them:
If you had known
that the Temple is destroyed,
would you have vowed nezirus?
They said to him: No.
And Nachum the Mede released them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life case where the before/after distinction from step 1 was missed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום המדי released the vows because of the Temple's destruction, which happened after the vows were made. The משנה calls this a mistake.

steps.title: The חכמים correct נחום: before the destruction, still a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ruled that whoever vowed before the destruction remains a נזיר. Whoever vowed after it is not a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the matter reached the חכמים, they said: Anyone who vowed before the בית המקדש was destroyed is a נזיר. Anyone who vowed after the בית המקדש was destroyed is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject נחום's ruling. They apply the same before/after rule as the stolen animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vowing before the destruction was not a mistake at that moment. A later event (a נולד) cannot undo the vow, so these people stay נזירים. Vowing after the destruction is like vowing after the animal was stolen: the vow rested on a false assumption, so it does not hold.
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is the moment of the vow. If the problem already existed then, the vow was a mistake and is void. If the problem came later, it is a נולד and does not undo the vow.

phrases.english: And when the matter came before the Sages, they said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁנָּזַר עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ — נָזִיר.
phrases.english: Whoever vowed before the Temple was destroyed — is a nazirite.
And after the Temple was destroyed — he is not a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns נחום's release from step 2, using the principle of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow made before the destruction stands. A vow made after the destruction is void.

steps.title: רבה: the חכמים won over רבי אליעזר about נולד
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the חכמים overpowered רבי אליעזר until he accepted their view. רבי אליעזר had held that a vow may be opened with a נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The חכמים overpowered רבי אליעזר and brought him around to their view. As we learned: 'We may open a vow with a נולד (a new development). These are the words of רבי אליעזר. But the חכמים forbid it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבה connects our משנה to a famous argument about releasing vows because of something that happened later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere, רבי אליעזר allows releasing a vow because of a later event (a נולד), and the חכמים forbid it. Our משנה refuses to release the נזירים over the later destruction, and no one disagrees. So רבה concludes that רבי אליעזר gave in to the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: they swept him along, overpowered him in argument
and brought him to their position
as we learned in a משנה
we 'open' a vow, finding a reason to release it
a new development that arose after the vow

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the accepted halacha: a vow cannot be released just because of an event that came after it.

phrases.english: GEMARA. Rabba said:
The Rabbis overpowered Rabbi Eliezer
and brought him to their position.
As we learned: We may open a vow with a new development,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדרים 64a. 'Opening' means finding a reason the person would not have vowed.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer,
and the Sages forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שַׁטְפוּהוּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's ruling in step 3 as evidence that רבי אליעזר took back his view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר accepted the view of the חכמים that a vow is not opened with a נולד.

steps.title: רבא: opening with the 'condition of a נולד' is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even though the חכמים forbid opening with a נולד, they allow opening with the 'condition' of a נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even though the חכמים said we may not open a vow with a נולד, we may open it with the condition of a נולד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes the rule of the חכמים narrower. Not every question about a later event is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What the חכמים forbid is asking about the new event itself. רבא says we may still ask about a 'condition' of it: the possibility of that event, which already existed when the person vowed. The next steps explain what this looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: with the 'condition' of a new development, meaning its possibility at the time of the vow

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even though the Rabbis said
we may not open a vow with a new development,
we may still open it with the condition of a new development.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבה's conclusion that the חכמים won, but adds a limit to their rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening with a נולד is forbidden, but opening with the 'condition' of a נולד is allowed.

steps.title: What does 'condition of a נולד' look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical picture of רבא's new category.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how 'opening with the condition of a נולד' actually works. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's phrase is new and unclear. The גמרא wants to know exactly what question the חכם would ask.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of רבא's rule in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording or method of opening a vow with the 'condition of a נולד'.

steps.title: The right question: 'If someone had told you…'
steps.stepSummary: The חכם asks: 'If someone had come and told you the בית המקדש would be destroyed, would you have vowed?'
steps.simpleTranslation: We say to them: 'If a person had come and told you that the בית המקדש would be destroyed, would you have vowed?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example. The question is phrased as if someone had warned them at the moment they vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question does not ask about the destruction as something that already happened. It asks whether a warning about it, given at the time of the vow, would have stopped them. Since the possibility already existed back then, this counts as a 'condition' of the נולד, and a 'no' answer lets the vow be released.
steps.confusionAlert: This question sounds almost the same as נחום's question in step 2, but it is not. נחום asked about the destruction as a fact that had already happened, which is a pure נולד. רבא's question asks about a warning given at the time of the vow, which is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow cannot be released over a later event itself. It can be released if the person would not have vowed had he been warned at the time that the event might happen.

phrases.english: We say to them:
If a person had come and said to you
that the Temple is destroyed,
phrases.notes: He means a warning given before the vow, telling them the בית המקדש would be destroyed.

phrases.english: would you have vowed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לְהוֹן: אִילּוּ אֲתָא אִינִישׁ וַאֲמַר לְכוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a concrete wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכם asks whether they would have vowed if someone had told them, at the time, that the בית המקדש would be destroyed. A 'no' answer opens the vow.

steps.title: רב יוסף's suggested opening from a פסוק in ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that if he had been there, he would have opened the vows by quoting a פסוק showing that both Temples would be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If I had been there, I would have told them: Isn't it written 'The Sanctuary of the Lord, the Sanctuary of the Lord, the Sanctuary of the Lord, are these'? That means the First Temple and the Second Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers his own way to release the נזירים who vowed before the חורבן. He would point to a פסוק that already told them the Temple would fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'היכל ה׳' three times, which hints at three Temples. That means the Second Temple was always going to be destroyed. So the destruction was not truly new or unexpected (a נולד), and it could be used to open the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary of ה׳; here, the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If I had been there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the נזירים who arrived and found the בית המקדש destroyed.

phrases.english: I would have said to them:
Isn't it written: "The Sanctuary of the Lord,
the Sanctuary of the Lord, the Sanctuary of the Lord, are these"
This is the First Temple and the Second Temple.
phrases.notes: Saying it three times hints at three Temples, so the first two were going to be destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לְהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different, stronger way to open the vow than the חכם's question in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The destruction was foretold in the פסוק, so it is not a true נולד and can be used to open the vow.

steps.title: Knowing it will happen is not knowing when
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's idea. Even if they knew the Temple would be destroyed, they did not know when.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that they knew it would be destroyed, but did they know when?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזירים could have known that destruction would come someday. But they could not have known it would happen in their own lifetime, before they brought their קרבנות. So their vow was not a mistake they should have foreseen.

phrases.english: Granted that they knew it would be destroyed,
did they know when?!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּיָדְעִין לְהוֹן דְּיִחְרוּב, מִי יוֹדְעִין לְאִימַּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from the פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק as grounds to open the vow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק tells that destruction would happen, but not the timing, so the נזירים could not have foreseen it.

steps.title: אביי: a פסוק in דניאל gives the timing
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that they did know when, because a פסוק in דניאל gives a set number of years.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Didn't they know when? But it is written: 'Seventy sevens are decreed upon your people and upon your holy city'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the גמרא's rejection by pointing to a פסוק that seems to give the date of the destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seventy sevens' means seventy cycles of seven years, which is 490 years. That seems to fix when the Second Temple would fall. If so, the timing was known, and רב יוסף's opening should work after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventy sevens: seventy seven-year cycles (490 years)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And did they not know when?
But isn't it written: "Seventy sevens
are decreed upon your people
and upon your holy city"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 9 that the timing was unknown.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the נזירים could not know when the Temple would be destroyed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in דניאל sets a fixed 490-year period, so the timing was knowable.

steps.title: Still, nobody knew the exact day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even with the number of years, no one knew the exact day of the destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, did we know on which day?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי. The year may be hinted, but the exact day was not known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the פסוק in דניאל gives the number of years, it does not give the exact day. So the נזירים could not have known the Temple would fall before they brought their קרבנות, and רב יוסף's פסוקים cannot be used to open these vows.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's attempt to open the vow from the פסוקים fails. Even with hints in the פסוקים, no one knew the exact day, so the נזירים could not have foreseen it. רבא's way of opening, with the 'condition of a נולד' (step 7), is not affected.

phrases.english: And still, did we know on which day?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 9 against אביי's challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the kind of knowledge needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Knowing the year of destruction would be enough to open the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only knowing the exact day would matter, and that was not known.

steps.title: New משנה: vows about a stranger on the road
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes travelers who each vow נזירות depending on who an approaching person is, or on whether the others become נזירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: People were walking on the road and someone came toward them. One said: 'I am a נזיר if this is so-and-so.' Another said: 'I am a נזיר if this is not so-and-so.' Others said: 'I am a נזיר if one of you is a נזיר,' 'if neither of you is a נזיר,' 'if both of you are נזירים,' 'if all of you are נזירים.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up a case of several conditional נזירות vows, and the next step brings the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two vows depend on a fact no one knows yet, the identity of the person. The later vows depend on whether the earlier speakers become נזירים. This sets up the question of whether a vow based on uncertain facts takes effect.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If people were walking along the way,
and one person was coming toward them,
one of them said:
"I am hereby a nazirite if this is so-and-so,"
and another one said:
"I am hereby a nazirite if this is not so-and-so,"
"I am hereby a nazirite if one of you is a nazirite,"
phrases.notes: From here on, each line is a new person speaking about the people who vowed before him.

phrases.english: "if neither of you is a nazirite,"
"if both of you are nazirites,"
"if all of you are nazirites."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ, וְאֶחָד בָּא כְּנֶגְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the discussion of the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out a case of several נזירות vows that depend on uncertain facts.

steps.title: Three opinions on who becomes a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say all of them are נזירים. בית הלל say only the one whose words were not fulfilled is a נזיר. רבי טרפון says none of them is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: All of them are נזירים. בית הלל say: Only the one whose words were not fulfilled is a נזיר. רבי טרפון says: Not one of them is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three opinions about the case of the travelers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that saying 'I am a נזיר' takes effect even if the condition was wrong. רבי טרפון holds that a vow made without certainty does not take effect at all, so even a correct guess makes no one a נזיר. בית הלל take a middle position.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds no one here is a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל's wording, 'whose words were not fulfilled', sounds backward. The גמרא raises this exact problem in step 16, and רב יהודה fixes the reading in step 17: only the one whose words came true is a נזיר.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: They are all nazirites.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ נָזִיר אֶלָּא מִי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּימוּ דְּבָרָיו.
phrases.english: Only he whose words were not fulfilled is a nazirite.
And Rabbi Tarfon says:
Not one of them is a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings for the case set up in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: all are נזירים. בית הלל: only the one whose words were not fulfilled. רבי טרפון: none are נזירים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument is about whether a vow based on a mistaken or uncertain fact takes effect, which the גמרא will go on to explain.

steps.title: If the approaching person turned back, no one is a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the approaching person turned back and was never identified, none of the travelers is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the person turned back, he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new case. The person the travelers were arguing about turned away before anyone could see who he was, so no one is a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every vow depended on who the person really was. Once he leaves without being identified, nobody's condition can be checked, and the משנה rules that none of them becomes a נזיר.

phrases.english: If he turned back,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person walking toward the travelers. He turned away before they could tell who he was.

phrases.english: he is not a nazir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more case to the travelers' משנה: the person is never identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the person's identity is never found out, none of the travelers becomes a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's formula: a נזיר either way
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says each traveler should declare that he is a required נזיר if his words were right, and a volunteer נזיר if they were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He should say, 'If it was as I said, I am a נזיר by obligation. If not, I am a נזיר by free choice.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the ruling just stated. He gives each traveler words to say so that he becomes a נזיר no matter who the person was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traveler does not know whether his vow took effect. By saying this two-sided statement, he is a נזיר in both cases: either because of his first vow, or because of a new vow he takes now. That way the doubt no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the ruling of the first opinion
As I said, according to my words
A נזיר by obligation, because his earlier vow took effect
A נזיר by free choice, a new vow taken on his own

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion says that when the person is never identified, no one is a נזיר. רבי שמעון gives a statement that makes each traveler a נזיר either way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He should say,
"If it was as I said,
I am hereby a nazir by obligation,
phrases.notes: He means: if my condition came true, I am already a נזיר because of my first vow.

phrases.english: and if not, I am hereby a nazir by free choice."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יֹאמַר אִם הָיָה כִדְבָרַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in step 14 and offers a practical way to handle the doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each traveler should declare himself a required נזיר if his words were right and a volunteer נזיר if not, so that he is a נזיר either way.

steps.title: Why would the one who was wrong become a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about בית הלל's ruling: why should the person whose words did not come true be a נזיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The one whose words were not fulfilled, why is he a נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It challenges the wording of בית הלל's view from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each traveler vowed to be a נזיר only if he turned out to be right. The person who was wrong never had his condition met, so it makes no sense for him to be a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; the discussion of the משנה begins here

phrases.english: GEMARA
The one whose words were not fulfilled,
phrases.notes: This quotes בית הלל's ruling from the משנה (step 13).

phrases.english: why is he a nazir?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּימוּ דְּבָרָיו אַמַּאי הָוֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to בית הלל's view in step 13 and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of בית הלל in the משנה: "only the one whose words were not fulfilled is a נזיר."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each vow depended on being right. The one who was wrong never met his condition, so he should not be a נזיר.

steps.title: רב יהודה: read it as the one whose words came true
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says to change the reading of the משנה: the one whose words DID come true is the נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Say instead, 'the one whose words were fulfilled.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by fixing how we read the משנה. In בית הלל's view, the נזיר is the person who was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem came from the word "not." רב יהודה removes it, so בית הלל now say the logical thing: only the traveler whose condition came true becomes a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
Say, read it as; used to correct how we read a text

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה is not inventing a new opinion for בית הלל. He is fixing the reading, so בית הלל rule that the one who was RIGHT is the נזיר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Say instead:
the one whose words were fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by correcting the reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that the traveler who was wrong becomes a נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read בית הלל as saying that only the traveler whose words came true is a נזיר.
